Lead strategic projects sponsored by the EMEA Leadership Team and Global functions. Identify opportunities to automate, simplify and optimize processes. Drive continuous improvement programmes that improve operational effectiveness and customer satisfaction. Represent EMEA in global business improvement, transformation and portfolio development initiatives. Make strategic recommendations to support long-term organizational effectiveness and growth. People leadership and capability development Lead, coach and develop a high-performing team across portfolio management, operational support and business improvement. Build a culture of accountability, collaboration, innovation and customer focus. Identify capability gaps and put development plans in place to meet future business needs. Lead onboarding, training and upskilling programmes that support revenue growth and operational resilience. Promote cross-functional collaboration and knowledge sharing across EMEA and other Assurance regions. Lead succession planning and talent development within the team. Leadership and stakeholder management Build strong working relationships across Sales, Operations, Technical, Marketing, Finance and Global functions. Use data and market intelligence to influence strategic decisions and contribute to regional growth, profitability and organizational effectiveness. Represent EMEA in global portfolio and operational initiatives. Proven experience developing and executing growth strategies. Strong commercial acumen, with experience managing revenue, margin, or business performance metrics. Demonstrable experience leading business improvement and transformation initiatives. Strong analytical and data interpretation skills. Proven experience leading and developing teams. Excellent stakeholder management and influencing skills. A strong understanding of customer needs, commercial drivers, and operational delivery. Experience working in complex regional or global matrix organizations. Excellent communication, presentation and project leadership skills. Desirable Experience in certification, assurance, testing, inspection or professional services. Product or portfolio management experience. A project management qualification. Experience working across EMEA organizations that operate in multiple countries. BSI Excellence behaviors Customer focus — Put internal and external customers at the center of your thinking. Communication — Build credibility and communicate effectively to help achieve organizational objectives. Achievement — Deliver results and create value. Leading and managing others — Engage, develop and empower your team to achieve individual and team goals that support the business. review_candidates.title: Director of Technical Sales & Applications – RF, Microwave & Millimeter-Wave
review_candidates.description: About HASCO RF HASCO RF is a specialized distributor of RF, microwave, and millimeter-wave components, supporting engineers, OEMs, and technology companies across aerospace, defense, space, satellite communications, radar, semiconductor, wireless communications, and test and measurement markets. Our product portfolio includes precision coaxial connectors, adapters, cable assemblies, attenuators, directional couplers, power dividers, amplifiers, mixers, frequency multipliers, antennas, waveguide components, and other high-frequency solutions. Operating under an AS9120B and ISO 9001:2015 certified quality management system, HASCO combines technical expertise, authorized manufacturer relationships, and responsive customer service to support customers from initial engineering development through production. About the Opportunity HASCO is seeking an experienced, technically driven sales leader to help shape the next stage of our company's growth. This position offers a unique opportunity to work directly with company ownership, influence strategic business decisions, develop manufacturer relationships, and strengthen our technical sales capabilities. The Director of Technical Sales & Applications will combine technical expertise, business development, strategic account management, field sales, and team leadership to drive profitable growth across HASCO's RF, microwave, and millimeter-wave product portfolio. This is a hands-on leadership position for someone who enjoys working directly with engineers, solving complex customer applications, developing new business, and mentoring sales professionals. The successful candidate will bring both technical credibility and commercial judgment, with the ability to translate engineering requirements into practical solutions and long-term business opportunities. We are looking for someone who wants to make a meaningful impact within a growing, privately held organization where individual contributions directly influence the company's direction and success. Key ResponsibilitiesTechnical Sales & Applications Serve as HASCO's senior technical sales resource, supporting customers and internal sales personnel on complex RF, microwave, and millimeter-wave applications. Interpret customer requirements involving frequency, insertion loss, return loss, VSWR, impedance, power handling, phase performance, mechanical interfaces, and environmental considerations. Recommend appropriate RF interconnect, passive, active, antenna, and waveguide solutions. Engage directly with RF design engineers, systems engineers, program managers, and purchasing professionals. Coordinate technical requirements and application challenges with manufacturer engineering teams. Support technical presentations, product evaluations, demonstrations, design reviews, and engineering design-ins. Business Development & Strategic Accounts Identify, qualify, and develop new business opportunities throughout the United States, with an emphasis on strategic OEM and engineering-driven accounts. Establish relationships with technical decision-makers early in the product development cycle. Develop strategic account plans that identify new programs, applications, and opportunities for expanding HASCO's market presence. Personally advance opportunities from initial engagement through technical evaluation, quotation, design-in, and production. Identify cross-selling opportunities across HASCO's extensive product portfolio. Conduct customer visits and develop meaningful relationships within aerospace, defense, space, SATCOM, UAV/UAS, radar, semiconductor, and other advanced technology markets. Sales Leadership & Team Development Provide senior technical and commercial leadership to HASCO's Inside Sales organization. Mentor sales personnel in technical qualification, customer engagement, product selection, and opportunity development. Establish effective pipeline management, forecasting, and opportunity review practices. Develop and deliver ongoing technical and product training. Improve sales effectiveness, quotation conversion, and customer engagement. Work with the President to develop the sales organization's capabilities, structure, and long-term growth strategy. Manufacturer Relationships & Product Development Strengthen relationships with HASCO's existing franchise manufacturers and strategic suppliers. Provide technical field sales coverage and support manufacturer growth initiatives. Identify and evaluate complementary RF, microwave, and millimeter-wave manufacturers for potential distribution partnerships. Assess new product opportunities based on technical differentiation, market demand, competitive positioning, and commercial potential. Support new product introductions, manufacturer onboarding, technical training, and market positioning. Provide actionable customer feedback and competitive intelligence to guide product portfolio development. Strategic Business Leadership Work directly with the President to develop and execute HASCO's technical sales and growth strategies. Contribute to strategic planning, market expansion, product development, and manufacturer selection. Identify opportunities to improve sales processes, technical capabilities, and organizational effectiveness. Collaborate with Purchasing, Marketing, Operations, and Quality to support successful customer outcomes. Help establish a scalable technical sales organization capable of supporting HASCO's long-term growth objectives. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Electrical Engineering, a related technical discipline, or equivalent RF and microwave technical sales experience. Minimum of seven years of experience in RF, microwave, millimeter-wave, or related technical component sales, applications engineering, or business development. Strong technical understanding of RF components, system applications, engineering specifications, and design-in processes. Demonstrated ability to originate, develop, and close engineering-driven business opportunities. Ability to communicate effectively with RF engineers, technical decision-makers, manufacturers, and commercial customers. Experience developing strategic customer relationships and managing complex technical sales cycles. Strong leadership, communication, presentation, negotiation, and organizational skills. Experience using CRM systems for opportunity management, pipeline development, and forecasting. Ability to travel domestically for customer and manufacturer meetings. Preferred Qualifications Ten or more years of experience in the RF, microwave, or millimeter-wave industry. Previous technical sales leadership, applications engineering, field applications, or business development experience. Experience working for an RF component manufacturer, authorized distributor, or manufacturers' representative organization. Established relationships within aerospace, defense, space, satellite communications, semiconductor, or test and measurement markets. Experience with precision coaxial interconnects, cable assemblies, RF passive and active components, and waveguide technologies. Experience developing manufacturer relationships, introducing new products, or expanding technical product portfolios. Demonstrated success mentoring and developing technical sales professionals. What Success Looks Like Success in this position will be measured through a combination of commercial growth, technical contribution, and organizational development, including: Incremental revenue and gross profit growth. Acquisition of new customers and strategic accounts. Development and conversion of qualified technical sales opportunities. Engineering design-ins that progress into production business. Strengthened manufacturer relationships and product portfolio expansion. Improved sales-team technical capabilities and quotation conversion. Accurate pipeline reporting and credible sales forecasts. Why Join HASCO? At HASCO, you will have the opportunity to contribute beyond the boundaries of a traditional technical sales position. As a senior member of our organization, you will work directly with company ownership and have meaningful influence over sales strategy, manufacturer relationships, product development, and the future direction of the business. This position is particularly well suited for an experienced RF industry professional who values autonomy, accountability, direct customer engagement, and the opportunity to build and develop an organization rather than simply manage an established corporate structure. As HASCO continues to grow, this position offers the potential for expanded leadership responsibilities across sales, commercial strategy, and business development. Approximately 20–25% planned domestic travel. Professional development and opportunities for expanded leadership responsibilities. HASCO RF is an Equal Opportunity Employer. review_candidates.description: Job Title: Chief of Party - USDA Food for Peace Non-Emergency Program - El Salvador Level and Grade: Senior Director | Grade 100 Job Type: Regular Full-Time Reporting Manager: Managing Director, Latin America and the Caribbean Business Unit: Latin America and the Caribbean Office: El Salvador Date: Anticipated award date The Organization About Corus: Corus International is the parent of a family of world-class social impact organizations that collaborate in the world's most vulnerable communities to deliver holistic and sustainable solutions to the interconnected challenges of poverty, access to healthcare, and climate change. Corus combines more than 150 years of experience from its nonprofit and for-profit affiliates - IMA World Health, Lutheran World Relief, CGA Technologies, Ground Up Investing, and LWR Farmers Market - to develop rural economies, eliminate extreme poverty, expand access to quality healthcare, and respond to urgent humanitarian needs in fragile contexts. Further details about the organization can be found at: https://corusinternational.org About Lutheran World Relief: Founded in 1945, Lutheran World Relief (LWR) partners with local governments, farmer organizations, private-sector actors, and communities to build sustainable, inclusive, market-based rural economies. LWR brings deep experience in agricultural market systems, food security, resilience, financial inclusion, value-chain development, producer organization strengthening, and private-sector engagement, including longstanding programming in El Salvador and across Latin America. Position Summary Lutheran World Relief is seeking a Chief of Party (COP) to provide overall vision, technical direction, and executive management for an anticipated USDA Foreign Agricultural Service Food for Peace Non-Emergency multi-year program in El Salvador. USDA has identified El Salvador as a priority country and announced that this programming will target people and places experiencing recurrent food crises through a Graduation through Agriculture-led Development Approach that combines the Graduation model, U.S. agricultural commodities, and targeted market systems strengthening focused on agricultural value chains. The program is intended to build resilience, improve food security, and reduce dependence on emergency food assistance. The COP will be accountable for the integrated design and delivery of a sequenced graduation and market systems strategy. The role will ensure that household-level support - including consumption support, coaching, financial inclusion, skills development, productive assets, and links to services - is deliberately connected to commercially viable agricultural opportunities, inclusive value chains, private-sector incentives, and durable local systems. The COP will lead the project team and consortium, serve as LWR's primary representative to USDA and senior Salvadoran stakeholders, and ensure high-quality, compliant, adaptive, and results-focused implementation. The position will be based in El Salvador and will report to the Managing Director for Latin America and the Caribbean. Regular travel to project areas is required. Actual hiring is contingent upon signed agreement and USDA approval. Salvadoran nationals are highly encouraged to apply. The scope aligns with Corus Senior Director | Grade 100, which covers full responsibility for all aspects of complex program implementation and senior external representation. Responsibilities Strategic and Technical Leadership Provide strategic, technical, and managerial leadership for the full program, ensuring a coherent theory of change and implementation strategy that integrates graduation, agriculture-led development, market systems strengthening, resilience, food security, nutrition-sensitive programming, and the use of U.S. agricultural commodities. Household and Graduation approach Lead contextualization and sequencing of the graduation approach, including transparent participant targeting, time-bound consumption support, household coaching and mentoring, savings and financial inclusion, technical and business skills development, productive asset transfer, and linkages to government, financial, social, and market services. Ensure that household graduation strategies are based on clear criteria and realistic opportunities for sustainable livelihoods. Agricultural value chains and market systems development Provide senior technical leadership for market systems development, including agricultural value-chain analysis, market actor and incentive mapping, private-sector engagement, access to inputs and services, finance, producer organization and MSME development, buyer-seller relationships, value addition, post-harvest systems, and enabling-environment constraints. Balance targeted support to highly vulnerable households with facilitative market systems approaches that avoid long-term distortion or dependency; use adaptive management to adjust sequencing, intensity, and partnerships based on participant trajectories and market performance. Program Management and Administration Lead annual work planning, budgeting, implementation, risk management, and performance reviews; ensure that technical, operational, financial, commodity, subaward, security, safeguarding, and human-resources functions operate as one integrated program. Ensure full compliance with the award, applicable USDA and U.S. Government regulations, LWR/Corus policies, Salvadoran law, safeguarding requirements, and donor branding, marking, reporting, and recordkeeping requirements; maintain strong controls to prevent waste, fraud, abuse, exploitation, and diversion. Build and manage a high-performing multidisciplinary team and consortium; define roles and decision rights, supervise senior staff, manage partner performance, resolve implementation bottlenecks, and foster an inclusive culture of accountability, learning, collaboration, and staff development. Ensure robust monitoring, evaluation, accountability, research, and learning systems that disaggregate results, track household graduation and market-system change, assess resilience and food-security outcomes, document unintended effects, and support timely course correction. Ensure timely, accurate, and high-quality submission of work plans, financial and program reports, indicator data, evaluations, learning products, and other deliverables; communicate implementation risks, decisions, and corrective actions clearly to USDA and Corus leadership. Oversee all aspects of U.S. agricultural commodity planning and integration relevant to the award, coordinating with qualified commodity, logistics, warehousing, distribution, and compliance staff to ensure commodities support program objectives and participant safety without undermining local markets. Supervisory Directly supervises the Deputy Chief of Party, MERL Director, and other senior project leadership positions established in the approved staffing structure. Education & Experience Master's degree in agricultural economics, economics, agribusiness, international development, food security, business administration, public policy, or a closely related field; a bachelor's degree with substantial additional relevant experience may be considered. Minimum 10 years of progressively responsible experience leading large, complex, multi-year international development or food-security programs, including substantial senior management responsibility for technical quality, personnel, budgets, partnerships, compliance, and results. Prior experience as Chief of Party, Project Director, Deputy Chief of Party, or equivalent senior leader on a large U.S. Government-funded agriculture, livelihoods, resilience, food assistance, or economic-growth program is required; USDA/FAS or legacy USAID Food for Peace DFSA/RFSA experience is strongly preferred. Demonstrated technical expertise in the Graduation Approach or closely related economic-inclusion programming, including participant targeting, consumption support, coaching, savings and financial inclusion, livelihood skills, productive assets, service linkages, and graduation measurement. Demonstrated expertise in market systems development and agricultural value-chain programming, including private-sector engagement, market analysis, business and financial services, producer organizations, MSMEs, market linkages, and strategies to address systemic constraints without creating dependency. Proven ability to integrate household-level graduation interventions with market systems facilitation in fragile, shock-prone, or food-insecure settings, and to manage the trade-offs between short-term stabilization and long-term commercial sustainability. Demonstrated experience managing food-security, resilience, and agriculture-led development programs that apply adaptive management and evidence to adjust implementation in response to shocks, participant progress, and market dynamics. Experience leading complex consortia and managing subrecipients, grants, contractors, and technical partners; demonstrated ability to align diverse organizations around shared results, quality standards, timelines, budgets, and compliance requirements. Strong financial, operational, and award-management skills, including experience overseeing large budgets, internal controls, procurement, subaward management, audit readiness, and donor reporting under U.S. Government rules and regulations. Experience with U.S. in-kind food assistance, commodity management, supply-chain logistics, warehousing, distribution, or market-impact monitoring is strongly preferred; the candidate must be able to supervise specialized teams responsible for these functions. Demonstrated ability to engage effectively with senior government officials, USDA and other U.S. Government representatives, private-sector leaders, financial institutions, producer organizations, local partners, and community stakeholders. Experience working in El Salvador or the Northern Central America region is strongly preferred, with a strong understanding of rural livelihoods, agricultural value chains, recurrent food insecurity, climate and economic shocks, migration dynamics, and public-private coordination in the Salvadoran context. Excellent leadership, negotiation, communication, analytical, problem-solving, and interpersonal skills, with the ability to lead multidisciplinary and multicultural teams and make timely decisions under complex operating conditions. Professional fluency in Spanish and English, including the ability to conduct high-level negotiations and produce clear technical and management documents in both languages, is required. Ability to travel regularly within El Salvador and internationally, as required, and authorization to work in El Salvador at the time of hire or ability to obtain such authorization. Physical And Mental Requirements The physical requirements needed to execute responsibilities may include bending, standing, walking, and regular travel to project locations. Essential mental requirements include learning new tasks, comprehending and retaining information, completing tasks independently, communicating effectively, exercising sound judgment, and using computer software to perform assigned tasks. Other Duties This job description is not designed to cover or contain a comprehensive list of activities, duties, or responsibilities. Duties, responsibilities, and activities may change at any time with or without notice. All positions are required to perform additional tasks assigned by the supervisor. Positions bound by contracts will not be changed without notice and approval. Working Conditions, Travel and Environment This position is based in El Salvador and requires regular travel to project areas and occasional international travel. The employee must be available outside normal office hours or on weekends as required. While traveling, the employee may be exposed to high-security-risk settings, basic living conditions, outside weather conditions, and infectious diseases. The selected candidate must have authorization to work in El Salvador at the time of hire or be able to obtain such authorization.
